options.text: Kant holds that we know appearances, things as experienced, not things in themselves

questions.explanation: The distinction being tested is between what the view says and what critics fear. Kant holds that we know appearances, things as experienced, not things in themselves. This is the position defended by Immanuel Kant. The claim that kant holds that we know things in themselves directly is a common mistake about the view, often described as "realist misreading of Kant". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: the thing in itself is puzzling. Noting what the position does and does not claim resolves the matter.
